brief: Speculators are hesitant to go fully risk-on, with the risk of higher yields potentially restraining that appetite. Stocks cannot break out to new highs without a fresh positive narrative, and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra release did not supply one. Yields remain elevated for good reasons (rising real growth expectations, reinforced by Friday's positive jobs data, and heavy AI-related investment) and bad reasons (fiscal incontinence and inflation). Speculators' risk-on attitude was earlier drowned out by the war, turning positioning risk-off. Net positioning between risk-on assets (Bitcoin, AUD, NZD, BRL, MXN, CAD) and risk-off assets (JPY, CHF, DXY, gold, VIX) is now flat, but reluctance to go fully risk-on persists amid general uncertainty tied to yield risk. After the jobs data there is probably some impetus for yields to rise further, though seasonality may limit the rise into year-end. JPMorgan's Treasury client survey shows an increase in shorts, and Treasury ETF outflows have jumped to rarely-seen levels. Short interest in the largest Treasury ETFs, IEF and TLT, has held steady, so the outflows are unlikely to reflect short-covering and can be taken at face value, supporting the case that markets are starting to price appreciably higher yields.
